timing: untimed; derive from real approved narration/captions only

spans.text: Open Mapping and choose Map Icon Legend.
spans.purpose: Actual Mapping page with the Map Icon Legend entry control.

spans.text: A call's marker follows its type and priority. A unit's marker follows its type and current status. A person's marker follows an applicable role and status. Staffing levels do not change the icon.
spans.purpose: Read the exact legend hierarchy and family definitions.

spans.text: Our fictional examples are the Warehouse alarm, Reserve Engine 51 and Matthew Casey. Keep their names visible while comparing symbols. The colors and artwork identify different things, so match a marker to its named entity before drawing an operational conclusion.
spans.purpose: Introduce three genuinely named operating-map subjects; one clear filtered view per entity.

spans.text: From Department Types, edit Structure Fire. The Map Icon selector supplies a built-in choice; Custom icon supplies the uploaded alternative.
spans.purpose: Actual reopened call type, name, selectors and stored preview.

spans.text: Choose File and select the training fire image. Read the Icon guidelines: supported formats are PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP, up to one megabyte. SVG is not supported. Compare Preview on Light map, Dark map and In a list. A bold transparent square stays readable when small.
spans.purpose: Chosen base file, format/size guidance, preview variants and visible Update.

spans.text: Choose Update, then reopen the form. Showing the current custom icon confirms the stored result, rather than just a selected file.
spans.purpose: Current saved icon,128×128 storage, Update and Priority map icons.

spans.text: Choose Priority map icons.
spans.purpose: Priority map icons entry is visible on the saved call type.

spans.text: Find the Urgent row. Priority and Map color describe the actual setting; Default shows its fallback. The file selected here happens to be named call-emergency, but it is being uploaded for Urgent. A filename does not change the call's priority.
spans.purpose: Urgent/High row and actual selected call-emergency.png; no filename/priority confusion.

spans.text: Use that row's Upload button. Icon saved and the image under Uploaded icon show the stored replacement; Remove is now available.
spans.purpose: Saved Urgent override with banner and Remove.

spans.text: The named Warehouse alarm now shows that replacement on Mapping. In the legend, Routine and Emergency still use the type's base image with their priority badges.
spans.purpose: Actual specific operating-map icon, then three-column family comparison.

spans.text: Open Units and check Reserve Engine 51. Its Type is Engine and its starting Status is Out of Service. Engine 51 is a different unit and remains Released in this recording.
spans.purpose: Full readable unit names/type/status; distinguish Reserve from Engine51.

spans.text: Edit the Engine unit type. Review Actions, which is set to Standard Actions, then choose the training image under Custom icon. Compare the light, dark and list previews before choosing Update.
spans.purpose: Selected unit-engine-base.png, Standard Actions, previews and Update.

spans.text: Reopen the definition to confirm the current saved icon. The reserve unit's map initially shows that blue base image with an unavailable badge. Changing an icon definition does not change the unit's status.
spans.purpose: Saved Engine base and initial Reserve map fallback; status comes from separate Units row.

spans.text: Open Status map icons for Engine.
spans.purpose: Status map icons entry is visible on the saved Engine type.

spans.text: Choose the Available row and select the green training image. Notice that Map color follows the operational meaning, while the status label has its own display color.
spans.purpose: Actual selected unit-available.png on Available; label/meaning swatches differ.

spans.text: Choose Upload and confirm Icon saved. This replacement applies to Engine units while Available.
spans.purpose: Saved Available row and distinct Uploaded icon.

spans.text: For the disposable reserve example, open Set Status, choose Available, keep Destination at None, add a clear training Note and choose Save.
spans.purpose: Foreground normal status dialog; no clipped note suffix or modal background counted.

spans.text: The Units grid confirms Available. The map then shows the green replacement. Its station point was supplied separately as declared simulated fixture setup. This dialog did not collect GPS or inherit station coordinates; an entity without a permitted location may have no marker.
spans.purpose: Saved normal status and real map after separately recorded simulated status-location append51020→51021.

spans.text: Open Personnel Roles and view Officer.
spans.purpose: Actual Officer row with View control.

spans.text: Matthew Casey, Stella Kidd and Christopher Herrmann are already members in this fictional department.
spans.purpose: Read-only actual role membership; no assignment mutation.

spans.text: Edit the role, choose the training image under Custom icon, inspect Preview and choose Save.
spans.purpose: Selected role-officer-base.png and actual Save.

spans.text: Reopen it to confirm Showing the current custom icon.
spans.purpose: Actual stored Officer icon confirmation.

spans.text: Back on Personnel Roles, read Role order. A person uses the first role they hold, in this order, that has an icon. Officer is fourth here. If you deliberately change the order, use Save order. No role order or membership is changed in this example.
spans.purpose: Existing ordered roles, rule text and Save order control; no ordering result claimed.

spans.text: From Officer, choose Status map icons.
spans.purpose: Status map icons entry is visible on the saved Officer role.

spans.text: Find Standing By and select its training replacement. This combination belongs to that role and that personnel status; it does not apply to every member regardless of role.
spans.purpose: Actual selected role-standing-by.png on Standing By row.

spans.text: Choose Upload and check Icon saved, Uploaded icon and Remove on the same row.
spans.purpose: Actual saved Standing By override.

spans.text: Return to the map and filter to Matthew Casey. The named marker shows the gray replacement from the Standing By row. Keep the visible name with the symbol so a nearby person's marker cannot be mistaken for Casey's.
spans.purpose: Actual named Casey marker matches replacement; clipped top controls excluded.

spans.text: Use Map Icon Legend to explain how a symbol is chosen. An upload for the exact priority or status wins. Otherwise the type's or role's own upload can carry a meaning-colored badge. Otherwise a built-in pin uses that style.
spans.purpose: Readable actual hierarchy and status/priority meaning examples.

spans.text: Compare the Structure Fire row across priorities.
spans.purpose: Specific Urgent replacement beside Routine/Emergency base+badges.

spans.text: Then compare Engine across statuses: Available has its specific replacement while the other states use the base and badge.
spans.purpose: Actual whole Engine family with state labels.

spans.text: Finally compare Officer across personnel statuses. The legend also explains that a member On Unit can take the color of their unit's status. That is a reference example here, not a newly performed crew assignment.
spans.purpose: Actual role family and On Unit explanation, without claiming unperformed assignment.

spans.text: Restore the disposable reserve unit through Set Status.
spans.purpose: Actual Reserve row with Set Status entry control.

spans.text: Choose Out of Service, wait for Destination to settle at None, add the training restoration Note and choose Save.
spans.purpose: Actual foreground restoration dialog; clipped note tail not transcribed.

spans.text: The Units grid confirms Out of Service, while Engine 51 remains Released.
spans.purpose: Actual saved restoration and unchanged separate Engine state.

spans.text: For this recording, the original fictional station point is restored again as separate simulated setup data. The actual map now shows the blue Engine base with its black unavailable badge, matching the legend. The status changes used the normal application controls; neither setup step demonstrates device GPS or an operational response.
spans.purpose: Actual final restored map after separate append51022→51023, then corresponding Engine legend.

spans.text: Test a reversible fallback by returning to Structure Fire's Urgent row and choosing Remove for this disposable override.
spans.purpose: Actual saved Urgent override immediately before normal Remove.

spans.text: Icon removed appears, and Uploaded icon returns to None. The call's priority has not changed.
spans.purpose: Actual removed banner and empty Urgent upload.

spans.text: Revisit the legend and the named Warehouse alarm. Both now show the base fire image with the high-priority badge. The original training calls remain open and unchanged. Finish by recording a small, consistent set of symbols and meanings, and retain labels where an icon could be ambiguous. These are actual Core browser views; native-device appearance is not demonstrated here.
spans.purpose: Actual legend/map fallback after removal; no call mutation or native/client result claim.

required_labels: Every scene label is covered by its exact reviewed screenshot union; entry-control spans are explicit and may be held through the first spoken instruction.
